findings.description: ablation-row.sh derives the row's `degraded`, `degraded_reason` and `voices_run` fields from the dissent envelopes at `$RUN_DIR/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-{review,audit}.json`. That path is inside the sandbox the model under test writes to. The harness explicitly refuses to read the arm from sandbox/ (DEC-0413) and tracks `.claude/` writes as zone violations, so the sandbox is already treated as semi-adversarial, yet the envelope lookup prefers the sandbox copy and only falls back to the harness-side `eval/adversarial-*.json` when the sandbox file is absent. A sandbox file that exists but is not a JSON object yields null without ever consulting the eval/ copy.
findings.failure_mode: An agent under evaluation (or a prompt-injected one) writes or overwrites the envelope with `verdict_quality.status: OK` and `voices_succeeded == voices_planned`, suppressing the DEGRADED flag and the voice-count check, or deletes it so `voices_run` reads null. The ablation then records a clean gate run that did not happen, corrupting the comparison the whole harness exists to make. The same concern applies to `eval/model-invoke.jsonl` if eval/ is inside the container's /workspace mount (pipeline-run.sh and lib/sandbox-mount.sh were truncated and could not be checked).
findings.suggested_fix: Have the gate runner (pipeline-run.sh) copy the envelope out of the sandbox into `$RUN_DIR/eval/` at phase end, and make ablation-row.sh read only the eval/ copy. If the sandbox copy must remain the source, record its sha256 in the row and compare against the hash the pipeline captured when the gate finished. Confirm eval/ is not under any mount the executor can write.

findings.description: The `--max-usd` spend cap is accounted solely from `.executor.total_cost_usd` in each finished row, which comes from the CLI's final `result` event. A trial that is killed on timeout, dies in transport, or produces no row has no result event, so `collect` adds 0 to SPENT (the regex fallback also maps any malformed value to 0). The `run_cap` reservation covers a trial only while it is in flight; once it fails its real spend is forgotten. Transport retries likewise carry only the final attempt's cost into the row.
findings.failure_mode: A batch in a degraded network or a model that routinely stalls past `timeout_per_trial_s` burns real API spend on every attempt while SPENT stays near zero. `budget_gate` keeps launching, so `--max-usd` is exceeded without any cut being recorded in STATUS.json. The operator believes they have a hard ceiling when they do not.
findings.suggested_fix: When a trial ends without a reported cost, charge it `run_cap` (the worst-case reservation) to SPENT instead of 0, and record `cost_source: assumed_cap` in the row. Alternatively, derive spend from the MODELINV / cost ledger (which cheval writes per hop) rather than the single CLI summary, so partial attempts are counted. Document in the header that the cap is advisory until this is done.

findings.description: `resolve_effort` ends in a `case` whitelist, but the cycle-130 arm override replaces `effort` with the raw jq string from the suite toggles after that validation and passes it straight to `--effort` on the CLI argv. This file performs no check that the value is one of low|medium|high|xhigh|max. The header says `apply_arm_toggles` (lib/sandbox-mount.sh, truncated from the diff) verifies the effort toggle, so correctness depends entirely on that library rejecting non-enum values before this line runs.
findings.failure_mode: If the library accepts any string (or a later refactor relaxes it), a suite entry like `effort: 'maximum'` or `effort: 3` runs the executor with an invalid flag value and the CLI either errors (lost trial) or silently falls back to a default, so the arm runs as its baseline without the exit-2 guarantee the header promises. The value reaches argv as a single element, so there is no shell injection.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-validate `arm_effort` against the same `case` list used in `resolve_effort` (or factor the whitelist into one function) and exit 2 on mismatch, independent of what lib/sandbox-mount.sh does.

findings.anchor: Write/Edit tool inputs under .claude/ from every transcript
findings.description: `zone_violations.dot_claude_writes` is computed by regex-matching `input.file_path` / `input.notebook_path` of Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit tool_use events against `(^|/)\.claude/`. It does not see writes performed through Bash (`echo > .claude/x`, `cp`, `sed -i`), writes through a symlink or hardlink whose literal path does not contain `.claude/`, or writes to the other mounted prompt-surface files (CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml, skills) that the arms toggle. execute-agent.sh restricts tools to Read,Grep,Glob,Write, but pipeline-run.sh (truncated) may grant Bash.
findings.failure_mode: An agent that edits its own instructions or re-enables a toggled feature via a Bash write or an aliased path produces a row with an empty violation list, and the ablation attributes the result to the arm rather than to self-modification.
findings.suggested_fix: Complement the transcript scan with a filesystem diff: hash the mounted `.claude/`, CLAUDE.md and .loa.config.yaml after mount_prompt_surface/regen_sandbox_manifest and again after the run, and record any changed path as a zone violation. Also match Bash tool_use commands that reference `.claude/`.

findings.description: The header states `gates: false` is implemented partly by exporting `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false` to the executor, and the new code unsets an inherited value only when `ARM_MODE` is true. In the non-arm path (no LOA_EVAL_ARM, the plain baseline eval), an inherited `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false` from the operator's shell passes through to the CLI environment untouched.
findings.failure_mode: An operator who exported the variable for a local debugging session runs a baseline eval that silently has gate enforcement disabled; the row records nothing about it, so baseline and treatment are compared on different footing.
findings.suggested_fix: Unset (or explicitly record) `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE` in every mode, and have `apply_arm_toggles` set it only when the arm declares `gates: false`. Record the final value in executor.json.

findings.description: When bats is not on PATH, fingerprint.sh falls back to executing a hardcoded path under the operator's home directory (`~/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats --version`). This bakes one developer's dotfiles layout into a shared harness script and runs whatever binary sits at that path on any host where it exists.
findings.failure_mode: On a shared or CI host the path may be absent (fine, reads `absent`) or may be a different user-writable file that is executed with the harness user's privileges when the fingerprint is computed. It also makes the fingerprint host-specific in a way the header does not document.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the home-directory fallback; use `bats` on PATH or `--bats-bin`/`LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN` only, and read `absent` otherwise.

findings.description: The arm written into the row is taken from the manifest's arm_map, else the first line of `meta/arm`, else pipeline.json, with only a non-empty check. execute-agent.sh enforces `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$` on LOA_EVAL_ARM, but ablation-row.sh does not apply the same pattern, and `--validate` only checks that `arm` is a string. The value is passed via `--arg` so there is no jq or shell injection.
findings.failure_mode: A corrupted or hand-edited meta/arm (or a manifest arm_map value with stray characters) produces rows whose `arm` does not match any declared arm; downstream aggregation (spend.sh, took-effect.sh, truncated from the diff) groups them under a phantom arm or drops them silently, and `--validate` passes them.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate ARM against the same regex used in execute-agent.sh and exit 2 on mismatch; in `--validate`, check `arm` against that pattern too.
